properties.state: {"concern":"core","designation":"internal","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"Usability is measured against a baseline, so getting harder to use is detectable","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"reflow2 regression-gates whether its DETECTORS still work and has no equivalent for whether a person or agent can still get THROUGH the process. tools/phase_trial.py seeds a realistic graph, injects the divergences P3/P4/P5 are each meant to catch, scores whether the graph noticed, sits at 13/13, exits 0 and works as a regression gate; the erosion trial asks the sharper version, whether the design still describes the system after N rounds of test-fails/fix-code/accept. Both measure the machinery. Execution was separated from evaluation: one agent drove the workflows BLIND — \"Agent B should NOT see expected outputs\" — while a second read the transcript afterwards, categorised what went wrong and found root causes rather than symptoms, asking of each \"why did this occur, how did it manifest, how frequently, what is the fix effort\".
